subject: Physics
question: A motor uses 500 J of electrical energy and does 400 J of useful work. Calculate its efficiency. After servicing, its efficiency is measured at 90 per cent. Comment on the change.
response_text:
Efficiency = useful energy output / total energy input × 100%
= 400 J / 500 J × 100% = 80%.

After servicing the efficiency rose from 80 per cent to 90 per cent, a rise of 20 per cent. More of the input energy now becomes useful work and less is dissipated as heat in the windings and bearings.

faults.step: rose from 80 per cent to 90 per cent, a rise of 20 per cent
faults.note: Prose relation (R9, quant): from 80 to 90 per cent is a relative rise of 12.5 per cent (10 percentage points); stated 20 per cent is outside the 5 per cent band and the 0.5-point floor. [computed: computed change 12.5 % vs stated 20 % (5 % band, 0.5-point floor) -> does not hold]
